page: The UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server built on KVM virtualization. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 x86_64 processor featuring 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 480.0 GB of system memory, which provides 10.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the server is equipped with two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs that deliver a total of 384 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external volumes.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong multi-threaded and memory performance. The Passmark CPU score reaches 88533.65, and the extended instructions test scores 132359.27, both placing in the top tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth for large blocks is also top-tier at 385.14 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 706.88 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 2168.19, indicating that the system's strength lies in parallelized execution rather than single-threaded speed.

This hardware configuration is highly suited for parallel processing workloads, including large language model inference, where prompt processing for a small model reaches 9458.91 tokens/sec. It is also optimized for high-throughput database operations, scoring 33288.64 in Passmark database benchmarks. The lack of local storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU VRAM and system memory relative to the vCPU count makes it a specialized platform for memory-bound and AI-focused workloads.
